opportunities.title: 1,000+ Bitcoin Miners Got Hijacked by a Fake Internet Route — and the Protocol Still Isn't Encrypted
opportunities.why_now: Braiins, The Block, and CoinDesk all confirmed the same BGP-hijacking attack on unencrypted Stratum connections within 24 hours, exposing an industry-wide blind spot.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown of BGP/Stratum hijacking with a blunt 'why is mining traffic still plaintext in 2026' thesis

opportunities.title: The Coldcard Bug Sat in Plain Sight for 5 Years — So Did Every Audit That Missed It
opportunities.why_now: Coldcard just published a postmortem admitting multiple security reviews failed to catch the flaw, a rare public confession from a hardware wallet maker.
opportunities.angle: Audit-theater takedown: what 'audited' actually means in crypto hardware, with a checklist readers can use on their own cold storage

opportunities.title: UK Regulators Discover DeFi Risk the Day After a $6.3B Hack Proved It
opportunities.why_now: The FCA's new DeFi rulemaking explicitly cites the Binance hack as justification, a textbook case of regulation arriving exactly one disaster late.
opportunities.angle: Regulatory-theater op-ed: map the timeline from hack to headline to rulebook and ask who it actually protects

opportunities.title: The CIA Got Hacked Too — and the Tool Was Named Artex
opportunities.why_now: A state-level intelligence breach using a named AI hacking tool just hit days after the Binance and 1Password incidents, signaling AI-assisted intrusion is now mainstream tradecraft.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on Artex plus a 'if the CIA can get popped, your multisig isn't special' framing for crypto holders

opportunities.title: 'Your Vault Is Safe' Is How Every Breach Starts Its Second Act
opportunities.why_now: 1Password confirmed names/emails leaked while vaults stayed encrypted, but Decrypt's own follow-up flags the real danger: targeted phishing against exposed users, a pattern crypto holders have seen before.
opportunities.angle: Security-led warning piece connecting metadata leaks to the phishing wave that follows, with concrete hardening steps for crypto users specifically
